conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning, Mr. Thompson. I'm Dr. Patel, one of your neurology team doctors. You're here for your second maintenance cycle of high-dose methotrexate for your CNS lymphoma.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good morning, Doctor. Yes, I remember. I’ve been feeling okay since my last treatment, but the eye floaters are back.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. You mentioned those usually improve after methotrexate. We’ll keep an eye on that. Any fevers, nausea, or other symptoms?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No fevers or vomiting. Just a little tired, but nothing too bad.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s good. We’ll start your IV fluids and bicarbonate today to protect your kidneys, just like last time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. Last time my liver numbers went up. Should I be worried?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re aware of that. Your dose was increased to 8 grams per square meter, which can affect the liver. We’ll monitor your labs closely.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thanks. I just want to make sure everything’s under control.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Absolutely. We’ll check your blood work daily. You’ll also stay on the special diet—no citrus, carbonated drinks, or vitamin C.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. No orange juice for me.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. We’ll start the methotrexate infusion this afternoon. Leucovorin will begin 12 hours after, a bit earlier than usual, because of your liver history.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Why earlier?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: To help reduce the risk of liver and kidney side effects. It’s a precaution based on your last admission.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That makes sense. I trust you all.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi Mr. Thompson. We just finished the methotrexate infusion. You tolerated it well—no nausea or discomfort?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, it was fine. Just a little anxious, but I’m okay.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good. We’ll keep monitoring your urine pH to make sure it stays above 8. That helps flush the drug safely.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Morning. Your labs from today show your liver enzymes are up—ALT and AST are elevated.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh. Is that bad?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s mild, and we expected it. It’s called transaminitis, likely from methotrexate. But your levels are already starting to come down.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So it’s not serious?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not at this stage. We’ll keep watching. Your kidney function is stable, which is great.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s a relief. My dad had kidney issues, so I worry.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I understand. We’re being extra careful, especially with your history of methotrexate-related kidney injury before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your methotrexate level was 4.8 this evening. That’s where we want it—coming down steadily.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So that means it’s leaving my system?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes. We’ll check again tomorrow. Once it’s below 0.2, you’ll be ready for discharge.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Great. I’d like to get home soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good news—your methotrexate level is now 0.24. Very low. We’ll do one more check later.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s excellent. What’s next?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re scheduled for a brain MRI today to check for any changes in your lymphoma.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will it show if the treatment is working?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes. We’re looking for stability or improvement. No new lesions or swelling.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The MRI results are back. There’s no change—your brain looks stable. The old lesion is still there, but no new tumors.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s good, right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, very good. It means the lymphoma isn’t progressing. We also want to follow up on your eye symptoms.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: The floaters are still there, but they fade after treatment.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll have you see the ophthalmologist again soon to check for ocular lymphoma activity.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Today we’re planning to give you a dose of rituximab as part of your ongoing treatment.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve had that before. Is it safe?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Generally yes, but we’ll go slowly. Some patients have reactions, so we’ll monitor you closely.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Mr. Thompson, during the rituximab infusion, you developed rigors—shaking chills. We stopped it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I felt cold all of a sudden. Is that serious?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It was likely a mild allergic reaction. We gave you solumedrol to stop it. You’ll now be on a prednisone taper for 18 days to prevent further issues.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Prednisone? I’ve heard that has side effects.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It can, but this is a short course. We’re using it to calm your immune system after the reaction.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I’ll take it as directed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your last methotrexate level was 0.24, now down to 0.41 and 0.81 in earlier checks—perfectly cleared. You’re ready to go home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. What about the prednisone?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll take 60mg daily for 3 days, then step down over the next two weeks as written. We’re also sending you home with docusate, senna, aspirin, and compazine for nausea if needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Same as before?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, no changes. Call us if you develop fever, worsening floaters, or any new neurological symptoms.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thank you, Doctor.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. We’ll see you in follow-up soon. Take care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: One more thing—should I avoid crowds because of the prednisone?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good question. Try to avoid sick people and large gatherings while on the higher doses, yes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. I’ll stay home mostly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. And keep drinking fluids, stay on your bowel regimen, and watch for constipation.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll do that. Thanks again for explaining everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Of course. We’re here for you. Have a safe trip home.
